44364406.article_content:
Updated on
June 17, 2025
in
#docker
,
#flask
Switching pip to uv in a Dockerized Flask / Django App
I noticed about a 10x speed up across a number of projects, we'll avoid using
a venv and run things as a non-root user too.
Quick Jump:
Prefer video? Here is it
on YouTube
.
I was surprised at how painless it was to switch things over. You can see the
git diffs to make the change for both of my example
Flask
and
Django
projects. In this post we’ll go into more detail about these changes and how to
use a few
uv
commands.
#
pyproject.toml vs requirements.txt
Let’s start with defining our project’s dependencies.
You can create a
pyproject.toml
file and delete your
requirements.txt
after
you’ve entered your project’s dependencies and their versions into
pyproject.toml
.
You only need to add your top level dependencies, uv will make a lock file for
you automatically which is somewhat comparable to what
pip freeze
would
produce except uv’s lock file has proper dependency trees and is way better.
Here’s a very small diff that shows an example of what to do, adjust it as
needed:
# pyproject.toml
+[project]
+dependencies = [
+  "redis==5.2.1",
+]
# requirements.txt
-redis==5.2.1
#
Dockerfile
It’s important that these steps happen in order. For example you’ll want the
environment variables defined before you install your dependencies.
Install uv
+COPY --from=ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:0.7.13 /uv /uvx /usr/local/bin/
Ensure both
uv
and
uvx
binaries are installed on your system’s path
Since uv is a compiled Rust tool we only need statically compiled binaries
You can find the latest release here:
https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/releases
Dependency Files
-COPY --chown=python:python requirements*.txt ./
+COPY --chown=python:python pyproject.toml uv.lock* ./
Reference uv’s dependency related files instead
That trailing
*
is important because it makes the lock file optional
The first time you build your project the lock file might not exist
Environment Variables
+ENV \
+  UV_COMPILE_BYTECODE=1 \
+  UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT="/home/python/.local" \
UV_COMPILE_BYTECODE
Python source files will be compiled to bytecode
This is preferred since all bytecode gets compiled once at build time
Your app doesn’t need to do this at run-time when the container starts
UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT
instructs uv to not make a virtual environment (venv)
My example apps run things as a non-root
python
user
Ultimately all Python dependencies will be installed in this path
Dependency Install Commands
-RUN chmod 0755 bin/* && bin/pip3-install
+RUN chmod 0755 bin/* && bin/uv-install
In both cases I extracted their install commands to a separate script so it’s
easy to either run at build time in the Dockerfile (as seen above), or by
running it as a command at run-time to make sure your lock file gets updated
on your host machine through a volume.
In any case, both solutions are just shell scripts. Here’s the one for uv with
comments:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set
-o errexit
set
-o pipefail
# Ensure we always have an up to date lock file.
if
!
test
-f uv.lock
||
! uv lock --check 2>/dev/null
;
then
uv lock
fi
# Use the existing lock file exactly how it is defined.
uv sync --frozen --no-install-project
There’s a few ways to use uv, such as using its pip sub-command but I like
using sync since it’s the “uv way” of doing things. The pip sub-command is
there to help create a mental model of how uv works, or continue using pip’s
commands through uv if you prefer.
The
--frozen
flag ensures the lock file doesn’t get updated. That’s exactly
what we want because we expect the lock file to have a complete list of exact
versions we want to use for all dependencies that get installed.
The
--no-install-project
flag skips installing your code as a Python package.
Since we have a
pyproject.toml
with a project defined the default behavior
is to install it as a package.
For a typical web app, you usually have your project’s dependencies and that’s
it. Your project isn’t an installable project in itself. However, if you do
have that use case feel free to remove this flag! You can think of this as
using
--editable .
with pip.
#
Add, Update or Delete Your Dependencies
If you’re using my example starter app, it comes with a few
run script
shortcuts. They’re shortcut shell scripts to run certain commands in a
container:
./run deps:install
Build a new image and volume mount out a new lock file
It’s mainly doing
docker compose build
and running
bin/uv-install
inside of a container which has a volume mount so your host’s lock file gets updated
./run deps:install --no-build
The same as above except it skips building but still mounts out a new lock file
./run uv [...]
It’s doing
docker compose exec web uv [...]
Execute any
uv
commands
you want, for example:
uv add mypackage --no-sync
Updates your
pyproject.toml
file and lock file but doesn’t install it
Then you can run
./run deps:install
This will either add a new dependency OR update an existing one
For adding, if you omit
==X.X.X
it will add the

data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对Amoeba分布式操作系统的回顾及其现代意义

不同观点：
• [sampo] 提到Amoeba操作系统与1992年Tanenbaum和Torvalds关于Linux的著名争论有关，并指出Amoeba有一个UNIX模拟器，但尚未完成。同时提供了运行Amoeba的硬件需求和相关链接。
• [haunter] 表示对Amoeba项目感兴趣，并提到Python语言最初就是为该平台开发的。他还分享了Amoeba源代码的存档链接，并发现了一个Github镜像。
• [killerstorm] 关注Amoeba系统的安全性，指出其安全性依赖于48位数字的不可暴力破解性，质疑这种假设的可靠性。
• [imglorp] 提出分布式操作系统研究在当前基础设施进步的背景下可能会有复兴的机会，并特别提到Kubernetes需要新的想法。
• [api] 认为过去关于分布式系统的研究被放弃了，提到了Mosix、OpenMosix、Beowulf等类似项目。他讨论了分布式操作系统的潜力和局限性，并提出无服务器架构可能是更好的解决方案，主张摆脱传统“盒子”概念，采用函数和事件驱动的架构。

补充讨论：
• [sodimel] 对Guido van Rossum曾参与Amoeba项目表示惊讶。
• [KingOfCoders] 回忆起Amoeba项目与自己硕士考试相关，带有怀旧情绪。

争议焦点：
• 分布式操作系统的安全性和实际应用中的局限性是讨论中的争议点，特别是不同硬件兼容性和性能差异带来的挑战。
• 分布式操作系统与现代无服务器架构之间的优劣对比，以及传统操作系统概念在现代计算环境中的适用性问题。

总结：讨论围绕Amoeba分布式操作系统的历史、技术细节及其在现代计算环境中的潜在复兴和应用展开，参与者分享了各自的见解和相关技术背景。

data.title: Microplastics shed by food packaging are contaminating our food, study finds
data.author: gortok
data.article_summary: 一项新研究发现，打开和关闭塑料瓶盖可能会将微塑料释放到饮料中。不仅仅是瓶装饮料，拆开肉类、预包装水果和蔬菜的塑料包装，以及打开牛奶或果汁纸盒时，也可能污染食物。玻璃瓶和带有塑料涂层金属盖的罐子也会释放微塑料。研究显示，每次开瓶，微塑料和纳米塑料的数量都会增加。这些塑料颗粒可能通过消化道或肺部进入血液，并分布到全身，可能带来健康风险。研究还指出，食品包装是食物中微塑料的直接来源，可能导致癌症、遗传突变和内分泌问题等健康问题。这一发现引发了对塑料污染和健康影响的广泛关注。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：塑料在食品包装中的使用及其替代方案，微塑料的来源与影响，以及责任分配和解决方案的讨论。

不同观点：
• **塑料包装的必要性与替代方案的讨论**：
  - **支持使用塑料**：gcanyon认为塑料在包装、存储和运输方面非常有效，替代方案可能更昂贵和不方便。superkuh进一步指出塑料可以保护食品免受污染和生物制剂感染，利大于弊。
  - **反对过度使用塑料**：ChaoPrayaWave提到即使购买有机或可持续食品，也难以避免塑料包装。kylebenzle则强调农业供应链已被塑料污染，土壤和食物中都发现了塑料。

• **微塑料的来源与影响**：
  - **多样化的微塑料来源**：taeric指出家庭中的微塑料主要来自衣物和干衣机的棉绒，而非明显的塑料包装。jakub_g分享了一项研究，发现玻璃瓶中的微塑料含量高于塑料瓶，可能源于瓶盖油漆。
  - **研究和数据的可信性**：roenxi对文章中的一些研究持怀疑态度，认为需要更多数据来评估塑料对健康的实际影响。zdenulo提到某研究链接无效，质疑其可信性。

• **解决方案与技术创新**：
  - **生物技术解决方案**：b0a04gl和whatsakandr提出训练土壤中的生物来分解塑料，或改造细菌以消耗微塑料。

Opening and closing plastic bottle caps can release microplastics into a drink, a new study found.
Cunaplus_M.Faba/iStockphoto/Getty Images
Food & health
Corporate news

Ripping the plastic wrap from the meat or prepackaged fruit and veggies you purchased at the grocery store may contaminate your food with micro- and
nanoplastics
, according to new research.
Plastic contamination may also occur when you’re unwrapping deli meat and cheese, steeping a tea bag in hot water, or opening cartons of milk or orange juice. Glass bottles and jars with a plastic-coated metal closure may also shed microscopic bits of plastic, the study found.
Garbage floating on the surface of the wate
Douglas Sacha/Moment RF/Getty Images/File
Human brain samples contain an entire spoon’s worth of nanoplastics, study says
In fact, the abrasion from repeatedly opening and closing the caps on glass and plastic bottles can release an untold amount of micro- and nanoplastics into the beverage, said Lisa Zimmermann, lead author of the study published Tuesday in the
journal NPJ Science of Food
.
“The research shows the number of microplastics increases with each bottle opening, so therefore we can say it’s the usage of the food contact article which leads to micro- and nanoplastic release,” said Zimmermann, scientific communication officer at the Food Packaging Forum, a nonprofit foundation based in Zurich, Switzerland, that studies chemicals in food contact materials.
Researchers have measured micro- and nanoplastics in such food and drink products as
beer
,
canned fish
,
rice
,
mineral water
,
tea bags,
table salts
,
take-out foods
and
soft drinks
, according to the study.
“This is the first systematic evidence of how normal and intended use of foodstuffs packaged in plastics can be contaminated with micro- and nanoplastics,” Zimmermann said. “We found food packaging is actually a direct source of the micro- and nanoplastics measured in food.”
A separate investigation by the Food Packaging Forum published in September 2024 found more than 3,600 chemicals leach into consumer products during food manufacturing, processing, packaging and storage,
ending up in the human body
.
Young woman sitting in a park, eating salad
Westend61/Getty Images
Common household plastics linked to thousands of global deaths from heart disease, study finds
Seventy-nine of those
food-processing chemicals
are known to cause cancer, genetic mutations, endocrine and reproductive issues, and other health concerns, according to the September 2024 study.
And while scientists have long known about potentially toxic chemicals from plastics leaching into food, “what’s less clear, and deeply concerning, is just how significant food packaging is as a source of exposure to plastic particles and what that means for our health,” said David Andrews, acting chief science officer at the Environmental Working Group, a Washington, DC-based health and environmental advocacy organization, in an email.
“This new study highlights food packaging and processing equipment as potentially significant sources of microplastic contamination in the food we eat, and ultimately in our bodies,” said Andrews, who was not involved with the research. “This study should raise alarm bells.”
CNN reached out to the Plastics Industry Association for comment but did not hear back before publication.
What are micro- and nanoplastics?
Microplastics
are polymer fragments that can range from less than 0.2 inch (5 millimeters) down to 1/25,000th of an inch (1 micrometer). Anything smaller is a nanoplastic that must be measured in billionths of a meter.
At 1,000th the average width of a human hair, experts say nanoplastics are so teeny they can migrate through the tissues of the digestive tract or lungs into the bloodstream. As the blood circulates, the plastics may distribute potentially harmful synthetic chemicals throughout the body and into cells.
Female hand taking bottle of mineral water from supermarket shelf
mediaphotos/iStockphoto/Getty Images
Nanoplastics linked to heart attack, stroke and early death, study finds
A flurry of recent studies have discovered microplastics and nanoplastics in human
brain tissue,
the
testes
and the
penis
,
human blood, lung and liver tissues, urine and feces, mother’s milk, and the placenta.
In the first analysis to illustrate harm to human health, a
March 2024 study
found people with microplastics or nanoplastics in their carotid artery tissues were twice as likely to have a heart attack or stroke or die from any cause over the next three years than people who had none.
Actions that worsen microplastic shedding
The latest research searched thousands of studies to find those that did the best job of identifying and measuring plastics in tested foods before narrowing the list to 103 for the review.
Microplastic research is quite new, and studies so far often use different methods of microplastic identificat

44364788.article_content:
A landscaper puts a cold towel over his head during a heat wave in Queens, New York City, on Monday.
Kylie Cooper/Reuters
Extreme temperatures
See all topics

New York’s Central Park tied a record high of 96 degrees for the date Monday, which was set in 1888. In neighboring New Jersey, 16 people were sent to the emergency room following a sweltering set of graduations. And in Baltimore, a malfunctioning Amtrak train left riders temporarily stranded without air conditioning in the depths of its tunnel system.
The staggering conditions come as an extremely dangerous heat wave is underway for the eastern half of the United States, with Tuesday expected to bring peak temperatures to an already fatigued population.
The potent
heat dome
reaches its peak at the beginning of the week, bringing the hottest temperatures of the year so far – the hottest in years for some cities – and putting tens of millions at risk.
Over 250
daily temperature records
could be broken during the peak of the heat on Monday and Tuesday, including both record highs and record warm lows. Temperatures in some locations from Philadelphia to Boston could be the hottest in any month in over a decade. Additional records could fall Wednesday and Thursday.
Around 150 million people were under heat alerts Monday, according to the National Weather Service. It feels more like July, summer’s hottest month, than June for many locations as temperatures rise 15 to 20 degrees above normal.
A level
4-of-4 extreme heat risk
is in place through at least Thursday, stretching from the Midwest to the Mid-Atlantic and including some parts of the Northeast. This long-lasting heat is rare and will likely offer little to no overnight relief, the NWS cautions.
Heat-related illnesses
increase significantly during extreme heat and can be life-threatening, especially for children, the elderly and people with pre-existing health conditions.
The dangerous impacts were immediate as sizzling conditions ramped up in the central US over the weekend and into Monday. Two graduations in Paterson, New Jersey, resulted in over 150 people being evaluated for heat-related illnesses, Paterson Fire Chief Alejandro Alicea told CNN, adding that the 16 people taken to the hospital were in stable condition at the time of transport.
A stalled Amtrak train in Baltimore left several passengers trapped in the heat for over an hour Monday afternoon.
“I honestly thought I was going to collapse on the train, and I’m fairly young and in good shape,” passenger Laura Evans told CNN. Even before the train stalled, Evans says several train cars did not have air conditioning at the start of the journey.
The train experienced “a locomotive malfunction,” Amtrak spokesperson Olivia Irvin said in a statement Monday night. “Passengers on Amtrak Train 94 were transferred to Baltimore Station and then provided train service to their final destination,” Irvin added. “Service recovery was initiated on board with snack packs and bottled water.”
In the nation’s capital, the Washington Monument announced it would be closed Monday and Tuesday due to an Extreme Heat Warning, an alert on the
National Park Service
website.
While the heat packed a punch Monday, the hazardous heat will reach a fever pitch Tuesday.
Heat remains the
deadliest form of extreme weather
in the US, and the frequency and longevity of
extreme heat waves are on the rise
in recent years due to human-caused climate change. Nighttime temperatures are taking the hardest hit from climate change, and are
warming faster than daytime highs
.
Over 48,000 homes and businesses were without power in Ohio, Pennsylvania, New York and New Jersey amid the dangerous heat early Tuesday, down from more than 100,000 Monday, according to
PowerOutage.us
.
Extreme heat also takes a toll on
infrastructure
, causing materials like concrete and asphalt to expand and warp. Problems were already cropping up in the Midwest over the weekend; parts of key thoroughfares in Milwaukee and Green Bay, Wisconsin, suburbs were closed after buckling under searing heat Sunday, local officials said. Similar scenes unfolded in Cape Girardeau, Missouri, and
the city warned
more streets could crack as the heat persists.
A road in Cape Girardeau, Missouri, buckled dramatically during a weekend of extreme heat.
KFVS
The skyrocketing temperatures have implications for rail and air travel, too. Trains powered by electrified wires typically have to run slower than usual as the heat makes the wires sag, leaving them susceptible to damage. Some Amtrak travelers in the Mid-Atlantic and Northeast could experience delays Monday due to “temperature-related speed restrictions,” the company said on
X
.
Brutally hot days can also make
takeoffs harder for aircraft
: Hot air is less dense than cool air, making the lift needed to send a plane into the air harder to achieve.
The temperature in New York City tied its daily record of 96 degrees Monday afternoon

data.title: SourceHut moves business operations from US to Europe
data.author: DyslexicAtheist
data.article_summary: Drew DeVault在sr.ht-docs中提出了第二版条款与隐私政策的更新。主要更改包括恢复之前过早删除的有关遵守美国法律的内容，直到其美国业务实体完全关闭。更新内容涉及隐私政策和使用条款文件的多处修订，如将"sr.ht"更名为"SourceHut"， clarifying用户信息处理方式，包括IP地址和会话cookie的存储。此外，还说明了用户数据删除的限制和原因，并提到了在使用付费服务时，支付信息的存储和保留期限符合欧洲法律要求。同时，API密钥的生成和存储方式也有所说明。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：隐私保护服务如何应对监管，特别是在跨国法律环境中的运作，以及对不同监管体制的信任问题。

不同观点：
• **reisse的观点**：认为隐私保护服务不应仅仅顺应当前政治正确的监管，而应像以前的盗版网站或现在的加密公司一样，利用各种手段逃避监管。他指出，如果用户信任某家公司，就应该信任该公司使用一切必要手段来保护用户，而不是依赖法律。他还认为，欧盟的数据保护法律虽然能保护普通用户免受大公司侵害，但对防范欧盟自身及成员国的风险无效。

• **jl6的观点**：对美国政府/科技巨头冰冷的自动化监管和本地强势人物的个人化干预哪个更糟糕表示不确定，暗示两者都有问题。jl6对不同监管体制的弊端提出质疑，认为在选择隐私保护服务时需要权衡这两种风险。

• **3D30497420的观点**：提到某公司在几年前已迁至荷兰，认为这是应对监管变化的一部分。这表明公司通过迁往法律环境更友好的国家来规避不利的监管。

• **tarkin2的观点**：关注实际操作问题，询问在欧洲的廉价VPS（虚拟专用服务器）推荐，要求公司和服务器都在欧洲。这反映了用户在选择服务提供商时对地理位置和法律管辖的考虑。

• **wyldfire的观点**：对某公司条款更新中加入“欧洲”一词的含义表示不确定，认为需要更明确的解释。这表明用户对公司政策变化的透明度和清晰度有需求。

• **bilekas的观点**：询问该事件的背景，特别是是否因为不认同美国的某项监管要求而做出调整。这反映了用户试图理解公司决策背后的法律和监管动因。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及公司如何利用跨国法律差异来保护用户隐私，以及用户在选择服务时对不同国家和地区监管环境的考量。
• 争议焦点在于公司是否应依赖法律保护用户隐私，还是应采取更激进的手段逃避监管。
• 用户对公司政策变化的透明度和明确性有较高需求，反映了在隐私保护服务中信息透明的重要性。

44365246.article_summary: Drew DeVault在sr.ht-docs中提出了第二版条款与隐私政策的更新。主要更改包括恢复之前过早删除的有关遵守美国法律的内容，直到其美国业务实体完全关闭。更新内容涉及隐私政策和使用条款文件的多处修订，如将"sr.ht"更名为"SourceHut"， clarifying用户信息处理方式，包括IP地址和会话cookie的存储。此外，还说明了用户数据删除的限制和原因，并提到了在使用付费服务时，支付信息的存储和保留期限符合欧洲法律要求。同时，API密钥的生成和存储方式也有所说明。
44365246.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：隐私保护服务如何应对监管，特别是在跨国法律环境中的运作，以及对不同监管体制的信任问题。

不同观点：
• **reisse的观点**：认为隐私保护服务不应仅仅顺应当前政治正确的监管，而应像以前的盗版网站或现在的加密公司一样，利用各种手段逃避监管。他指出，如果用户信任某家公司，就应该信任该公司使用一切必要手段来保护用户，而不是依赖法律。他还认为，欧盟的数据保护法律虽然能保护普通用户免受大公司侵害，但对防范欧盟自身及成员国的风险无效。

• **jl6的观点**：对美国政府/科技巨头冰冷的自动化监管和本地强势人物的个人化干预哪个更糟糕表示不确定，暗示两者都有问题。jl6对不同监管体制的弊端提出质疑，认为在选择隐私保护服务时需要权衡这两种风险。

• **3D30497420的观点**：提到某公司在几年前已迁至荷兰，认为这是应对监管变化的一部分。这表明公司通过迁往法律环境更友好的国家来规避不利的监管。

• **tarkin2的观点**：关注实际操作问题，询问在欧洲的廉价VPS（虚拟专用服务器）推荐，要求公司和服务器都在欧洲。这反映了用户在选择服务提供商时对地理位置和法律管辖的考虑。

• **wyldfire的观点**：对某公司条款更新中加入“欧洲”一词的含义表示不确定，认为需要更明确的解释。这表明用户对公司政策变化的透明度和清晰度有需求。

• **bilekas的观点**：询问该事件的背景，特别是是否因为不认同美国的某项监管要求而做出调整。这反映了用户试图理解公司决策背后的法律和监管动因。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及公司如何利用跨国法律差异来保护用户隐私，以及用户在选择服务时对不同国家和地区监管环境的考量。
• 争议焦点在于公司是否应依赖法律保护用户隐私，还是应采取更激进的手段逃避监管。
• 用户对公司政策变化的透明度和明确性有较高需求，反映了在隐私保护服务中信息透明的重要性。

data.title: Svalboard: Datahand Lives
data.author: morganvenable
data.article_summary: Svalboard Lightly是一款高度可定制的人体工学键盘，采用磁光按键技术，提供轻盈且触感良好的打字体验，有效减少手部疲劳。其独特的适配系统可根据手型调整，适合各类用户。产品提供多种指向设备选项，如轨迹球、指点杆和触控板，并支持多种安装方式。键盘布局完全可定制，兼容QWERTY、Dvorak和Colemak等布局，使用Vial-QMK引擎进行实时调整。Svalboard设计坚固，易于清洁和维修，所有机械部件均可通过3D打印制作，确保长期使用和修改。这款键盘旨在帮助减轻因打字导致的颈肩问题，提升舒适度和工作效率。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Svalboard键盘（及其前身Datahand键盘）的功能、可定制性、价格以及使用体验。

不同观点：
• inanutshellus认为Svalboard继承了Datahand的优点，且价格更加亲民。他提到自己25年前为了购买Datahand省吃俭用，而现在Svalboard不仅价格更低，还增加了轨迹球等新功能。他对该项目感到非常兴奋。
• morganvenable是从Datahand过渡到Svalboard的用户，他亲自参与了Svalboard的设计和构建，强调其在键盘和鼠标功能整合上的创新性，尤其是其高度可定制性和低操作 effort。他还提到有一个活跃的Discord社区供用户交流。
• nicoty关注的是键盘的多键操作能力，特别是是否可以在对角线上同时按下多个键，比如Q和Z。
• ilc分享了自己作为志愿者的经历，帮助Svalboard进行固件更新和调试。他指出自己从Glove80的Discord了解到Svalboard，并对其功能扩展和社区支持表示肯定。

补充讨论：
• heikkilevanto提出是否可以单独购买一个键盘并通过系统调整来切换左右手使用，他设想了一个便携式旅行工作站的配置。
• treeform刚入手Svalboard，提到其学习曲线和高度可定制性，并形容使用体验如置身于赛博朋克小说中。
• 0_gravitas是Glove80的用户，对Svalboard的可调节集群功能表示兴趣，但也提到自己的小手可能在使用这类键盘时有些不适，他希望有小手用户能分享使用体验。
• neves对视频演示中65 WPM的打字速度感到不满，认为作为演示视频这个速度不够理想。
• shocks和munro只是简单分享了自己对即将收到产品和相关视频的期待和信息。
• tecleandor觉得Svalboard的价格对于定制键盘来说过高，超出了他的预算。
• comrade1234分享了一个与主题相关的趣闻，提到有人通过使用不寻常的工具（如大羽毛笔）避免职场晋升。
• PaulDavisThe1st用幽默的方式强调了Svalboard对各种手部特殊情况（如手指受伤或不对称）的适应性。

争议焦点：
• 打字速度：nahuel0x质疑演示视频中的65 WPM打字速度是否足够快，以体现Svalboard的效率。
• 价格问题：部分用户如tecleandor认为Svalboard的价格偏高，而其他用户如 inanutshellus 则认为相较于25年前的Datahand，Svalboard已经变得更加实惠。

整体来看，评论主要围绕Svalboard的功能、使用体验和价格展开，多数用户对其创新性和可定制性表示肯定，但也存在对打字速度和价格的争议。

svalboard

Banish pain with the most adaptable ergonomic keyboard and mousing instrument ever made.

Magnetic = Light + Tactile
Lightly
brings fifty perfectly light, perfectly tactile magneto-optical keys to your fingertips, with integrated pointing for completely hands-down operation.

Custom Anatomical Fitment
The unique Svalboard fitment mechanism gives a perfect fit for any adult hand, accommodating finger length, fingertip size and palm size variation.

Life-changing Results
"Over the past six months, the Svalboard has transformed the way I work, helping alleviate my neck and shoulder issues by allowing me to type without strain.  Svalboard isn’t just another keyboard—it’s a game-changer for comfort and productivity."
- Jan Lunge
Watch Jan's video and more
Mount Anywhere
Built with a ~15° tent angle and M5 tenting screw inserts for extra tenting. It also has 1/4"-20 inserts for additional mounting options: chair-mount, lap desk, keyboard tray and Magic Arm compatible. Pictured here with
SmallRig Rosette 11" Magic Arms
Multiple Pointing Options
Trackball, Trackpoint, and now:  Touchpad!
Mix-and-match these integrated pointing devices for maximum comfort.
Buy now
Self-Print Kit Option
Print and assemble your own with our self-print kit and great community support.
Buy it here
Buy Now
Join the Discord
QWERTY and custom layouts
QWERTY
touch typers start with their fingers on the home-row:
A,S,D,F
for the left hand and
J,K,L,;
for the right hand. On Svalboard these are exactly the same. Your fingers rest on the round center keys of each key cluster. Then the
G
and
H
are simply inward flicks of the index fingers. The remaining four letters:
T, Y, B
and
N
are assigned new positions, becoming inward flicks of the middle and ring fingers. The thumb keys switch between different layers: (1)
Letters
, (2)
Numbers
, (3)
Functions
and (4)
Navigation
.
Alternative layouts like
Dvorak
or
Colemak
are easy to set up because the Svalboard Lightly is infinitely customizable. It uses
Vial-QMK
to change keys in real-time with no flashing required.
Learn more about Layouts
Perfect fit for any hand
Big hands?  Small hands?  Wonky finger lengths?  Broke a pinky when you were three and now it's all janky?
We've got you.
Individual 5-axis finger and thumb adjustability for natural hand posture.
3 axis palmrest adjustability for ultimate comfort and hand sizing.
1/4"-20 mounting hardware for tenting, chair and clamp-on mounting using standard camera hardware or just M5 screw inserts for tenting legs.
Buy Now
Light, small, tactile
No more springs or lubed switches. Svalboard's keys are light 20gf magneto-optical keys that have a 100% front-loaded force profile and a clean breakaway unlike anything else on the market. Fingers move just a few mm for any keypress. This reduces hand workload and fatigue by ~90% vs traditional keyboards, even "ergonomic" ones.
No more contortions or reaches to hit the keys at the edge of your keyboard.
Learn More
100% Customizable layout
Built on the amazing QMK engine, with massive community support.
Default QWERTY, Colemak and Dvorak layouts included.
Remap keys, layers, macros, combos, and use tap-dance functions -- all without reflashing thanks to the magic of Vial.
Learn about Vial
From the creator:
"As a Datahand user of 20+ years, I can safely say that Datahand saved my career.  I've tried everything over the years, and there's simply no comparison. When the company died, I was gutted.  When one of my precious Datahand units got damaged during travel, I got serious about building a replacement.
It was around then I found out about Ben Gruver's amazing
lalboard
design and built one myself, with lots of help from him.
Lalboard laid the foundation of basic key mechanisms which enabled Svalboard to come to life, but... it was not a production-oriented design.  With my background in high volume consumer electronics and input tech development, I decided it was time for me to dive in and make it a reality.
Like Datahand. I hope Svalboard will help thousands of RSI sufferers like me enjoy a faster, safer, more precise, and most of all PAIN FREE typing experience."
Built for the long now
In the spirit of the Svalbard Global Seed Vault, we're committed to a living design which can always be repaired, updated and modified by product owners.
All mechanical parts can be produced on a hobby-grade 3D printer, from SLA, or CNC'd from any material you like.
All pinouts are available if you want to hack your own electrical modifications, too.
Join the Discord
Robust and maintainable
In the proud tradition of the Datahand, we've designed Svalboard to be robust, easy-to-clean, and repairable.
Unlike Datahand, Svalboard is totally modular, for easy repairs and modifications.
There are no electromechanical contacts to wear out.
Keys are easily removable for cleaning.
Did we mention you can make your own replacement/custom-fit part

data.title: Show HN: Weather Watching
data.author: walz
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：图像识别技术的应用及其引发的隐私、技术实现和伦理问题的讨论

不同观点：
• cgsmith：认为图像识别技术很简洁有效，但同时对普遍监控的现象感到不安，担心隐私问题。
• eber：对使用图像识别技术来决定日常穿着表示支持，认为这在天气变化不定的日子特别有用。
• roxolotl：提到在影视作品中出现的技术如今已变得廉价和普遍，感叹技术发展的迅速。
• heeton：以幽默的方式描述了观看路人活动的体验，对互联网技术的发展表示惊叹。
• keyle：认为系统能正确识别路人穿着很有趣，但也指出系统无法识别潜在的犯罪行为，并提出开源该解决方案的建议。
• jackthetab：对技术实现细节感兴趣，希望有教程来了解如何实现这种系统。
• wiether：联想到一首歌曲，表现出对这种技术创意的喜爱。
• icameron：通过数据分析指出人们对穿着和文化的假设，并提到系统识别错误的可能性。
• okokwhatever：认为隐私问题已经是无法挽回的败仗，表现出对隐私问题漠不关心的态度。
• dylan604：关注系统的技术细节，质疑系统的健壮性，尤其是面对恶意干扰时的表现，如重复计数或遮挡物问题。
• ravdar：对该技术在未来广泛应用的前景表示乐观。
• cryptozeus：简单表达了对创意的喜爱。

补充讨论：
- 争议的焦点主要集中在隐私问题上，部分用户如cgsmith和okokwhatever对普遍监控表示担忧，而其他用户如eber和roxolotl则对技术的应用持积极态度。
- 技术实现和系统健壮性是另一个讨论重点，jackthetab和dylan604对技术细节和系统应对恶意干扰的能力表示关注。
- 伦理问题也被提及，如keyle提到系统无法识别犯罪行为，这可能影响其应用价值。
- 总体上，用户对技术的发展和应用前景持不同态度，有的表示惊叹和支持，有的则表达了隐私和伦理方面的担忧。

data.title: The No Space for Bezos movement: 'One man rents a city for three days? '
data.author: rguiscard
data.article_summary: 文章报道了亚马逊创始人杰夫·贝索斯即将在意大利威尼斯举行婚礼，引发当地活动人士不满并发起“贝索斯无立足之地”运动。活动人士批评贝索斯极度财富让他可以“租下”整个城市三天，而他的亚马逊则导致数千家意大利小商店关闭。运动组织在威尼斯多处悬挂抗议横幅，包括在圣乔治马焦雷教堂钟楼和里阿尔托桥上。运动不仅挑战贝索斯的奢华婚礼，还试图引发关于财富不平等和资本主义影响的讨论。活动人士成功将媒体关注从婚礼的奢华转移到对贝索斯财富和影响的质疑上，展现出对精英阶层无限购买力的反抗。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对杰夫·贝索斯在威尼斯举办婚礼及更广泛的反对游客情绪的抗议活动

不同观点：
• [randycupertino] 认为这次婚礼抗议是更广泛的“反游客”情绪的一部分，很多人借此机会表达对游客涌入的不满。
• [elcritch] 指出威尼斯本身通过历史上的不道德行为（如背叛拜占庭帝国和洗劫君士坦丁堡）获得了财富和艺术，现在居民却抱怨超富有人群租用城市享受这些历史艺术，具有讽刺意味。
• [noitamroftuo] 引用了 Heather Jane Johnson 的例子，认为她将个人经历与对亚马逊和贝索斯的批评联系起来是有道理的，并提出消除亿万富翁的一种方式是停止使用他们的产品。
• [xhkkffbf] 引用“No Big Ships”反游轮、反游客运动，并讽刺“No One Is Illegal”运动中对游轮游客的排斥，认为这种逻辑存在矛盾。
• [meepmorp] 以幽默方式评论，认为如果是埃隆·马斯克而非贝索斯结婚，可能会更有趣，因为可以联想到DOGE回归威尼斯。
• [southernplaces7] 对“No Space for Bezos”活动组织如 Laboratorio Occupato Morion 持批评态度，认为这些激进组织往往难以进行理性对话，并将其与极端右翼群体如特朗普支持者相比较，指出人类容易部落化并表现出原始倾向。

补充讨论：
• [philipallstar] 简要总结了 Guardian 文章内容，指出贝索斯从原本对民主党的支持转向对特朗普的支持，暗示政治立场变化可能也是抗议的原因之一。

争议焦点：
• 威尼斯居民对超富有人群租用城市举办婚礼的抗议是否合理，特别是在威尼斯自身历史上存在不道德行为的情况下。
• 激进组织如“No Space for Bezos”的活动是否能够进行理性对话，以及这些组织在抗议中的角色和动机。
• 个人对亿万富翁如贝索斯的批评是否合理，特别是与个人经历和经济行为如使用亚马逊产品的关系。

A banner in Piazza San Marco, Venice.
Photograph: Yara Nardi/Reuters
View image in fullscreen
A banner in Piazza San Marco, Venice.
Photograph: Yara Nardi/Reuters
Jeff Bezos
Inside the No Space for Bezos movement: ‘One man rents a city for three days? That’s obscene’
The Amazon boss, Jeff Bezos, is about to descend on Venice with his fiancee, some ex-Marines and his limitless credit card. We meet the Italian activists who are saying: enough
Zoe Williams
Tue 24 Jun 2025 05.00 EDT
Share
W
hen she heard that
Jeff Bezos
was getting married in Venice this June, Heather Jane Johnson felt worse than she had in her entire life. Twenty-five years ago, she ceased trading as a bookseller in Boston, Massachusetts. “I lost a lot because of Bezos and the complicity of Americans in the making of Amazon,” the 53-year-old says. “A big reason I moved to Italy is because I felt betrayed by my countrypeople.”
So when posters went up calling a public meeting in the city she now calls home, she went, and she has been to every meeting of anti-Bezos activists since, including one the day before her own wedding last week. “These young people have really restored my faith in humanity,” Johnson says.
Many of the No Space for Bezos activists are based in Laboratorio Occupato Morion, which describes itself as an “anti-fascist, anti-capitalist, anti-racist and trans-feminist political space”. “Let’s say that this is the house of many struggles,” says Federica Toninello, 33. It has the same vaulted ceiling and grand proportions as its neighbours, but is full of banners and placards, ready to festoon Venice for Bezos’s wedding celebrations, which are due to start on Thursday. (I spotted no billionaires when I visited on Sunday, but then they have a powerful drive towards invisibility.) It could be any countercultural collective, except this is Venice, so everything is a hundred times more beautiful. Striking, timeless graphics from past campaigns plaster the walls – No Big Ships, an anti-cruise, anti-tourist campaign, which started here before spreading across Europe; No One Is Illegal, a grassroots refugee solidarity movement; posters on the climate crisis, the housing shortage, and one from a pop-up feminist union representing the city’s maids.
View image in fullscreen
‘I don’t think he is welcome’ … Bezos with his fiancee, Lauren Sánchez.
Photograph: Bruce Glikas/WireImage
Noemi Donà, 19, is from the USG (loosely, the union of left youth); Oliver, 43, came via
the “Sardines”
, an anti-racist group set up to fight the hard-right Lega Nord. He works as a receptionist in a Venice hotel – not one of the hyper-luxe ones, just “a small, 14th-century palace” – but has his eye on the economy beyond tourism. “Bezos can pay, he can stay,” he says, “but thousands of shops in Italy have closed because of Amazon. So I don’t think he is welcome.” There’s a university collective that meets here, which occupied a number of campuses last year, protesting about the Israeli bombardment of Gaza.
The air is delicious and a bit headachey with the smell of aerosol and felt-tip pens. Some banners say Free Palestine; others say Stop Bombing Iran. Palestina Libre is an active organisation across
Italy
, and the US’s attack on Iran is still less than 24 hours old and deeply shocking. But if No Space for Bezos – “it’s not a collective, it’s a platform”, says Marta Sottoriva, a 34-year-old secondary school teacher – has ambitions that feel unimaginably large, it has already achieved some of what it wants, after only a few weeks.
“If Bezos had announced his marriage here, and we hadn’t moved, the narrative in the world’s media would have been the luxury hotels, the VIPs, the dresses, the gossip,” says Sottoriva. “We really wanted to problematise the ridiculous and obscene wealth that allows a man to rent a city for three days.”
On 12 June, the movement unfurled its simplest and largest banner – eight metres long, featuring just Bezos’s name crossed out in red – down the bell tower of the San Giorgio Maggiore basilica, while the deeply unpopular city mayor, Luigi Brugnaro, was trying to do a press conference. Toninello laughingly describes their slanging match on social media: “He was saying, ‘For shame!’ and we were saying, ‘
You
should be ashamed!’” Activists put up a similar banner on the Rialto bridge in the same week.
View image in fullscreen
The protest at San Giorgio Maggiore.
Photograph: Marta Sottoriva
They have already shifted the focus from: “How much money does that one man have?” to the more interesting: “How much disruption can No Space for Bezos cause? What kind of numbers will they get? What conversations will they start?” Between Elon Musk
handing voters million-dollar cheques
and Vladimir Putin ordering up chaos and death like consumables, there is this awful sense of limitlessness to the elite’s purchasing power. If it turned out there was something a billionaire couldn’t buy, and it was something that ought to be simple – a little goodwill, servi

不同观点：
• [VladVladikoff] 担心在疫情期间，一些收银员可能持续使用洗手液后接触含有BPA/BPS的收据，这会增加BPA或BPS通过皮肤吸收的风险。他同时担心这类信息可能给这些人带来压力。

• [incomingpain] 指出大多数美国主要零售商大约十年前就开始用BPS替代BPA，但这种替代可能同样有害。这表明了企业应对化学物质问题的一种常见策略——用一种可能同样有害的物质替代。

• [Simulacra] 提到一个与热敏收据纸褪色相关的实际问题，收据在一段时间后会消失，这尤其影响到产品保修。该用户的朋友曾游说国会取消这种收据纸，反映出对长期保存记录的需求。

• [4gotunameagain] 提出了一个有争议的观点，即研究BPA暴露是否与孕期中增加的跨性别儿童风险有关，尤其是男性后代。该用户强调自己并不是说一定有联系，但认为值得研究，并预见到会因为这个观点受到批评。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于BPA/BPS的替代问题以及其对健康的潜在影响，尤其是对特定人群如收银员和孕妇的影响。
• 另一个讨论点是热敏纸的实际使用问题，如褪色导致的保修困难，反映出技术选择对消费者权益的影响。
• [4gotunameagain] 的评论可能引发争议，因为它涉及一个敏感的科学和社会话题，即环境因素与性别认同之间的关系。

data.title: How to Care About Your Job When It Doesn't Care About You
data.author: mrmatthogg
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了在职场中，员工与雇主之间的权力不平衡问题。雇主通常将员工视为实现组织目标（如利润或公共服务）的工具，而非关心个体。即便员工努力做出贡献并期望从中获得薪水、经验等回报，组织往往只把员工当作数字或资源，而非真正关心他们的发展或福祉。文章指出，组织的决策往往是次优的，因为它们是由多个人共同做出的，而非单一理性个体，因此许多决定看似愚蠢或不合理。员工在面临升职缓慢、加薪不明等问题时，常感到挫败，而公司可能随时进行裁员，即便公司盈利良好。文章建议，面对这种不公，员工应调整心态，不必过度解读公司行为，以避免心理压力，并认识到职场中的“冷酷现实”。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：职场自由、自我管理理念、职场信任与承诺、企业裁员与人工智能的影响

不同观点：
• [artofpongfu] 认为工作本质上是不稳定的，人们随时可能因为各种原因陷入困境，比如糟糕的老板、健康问题或经济衰退。因此，他的观点是需要尽一切可能实现财务自由，或者至少具备在必要时离开的能力，而不是通过不断面试来维持职业稳定。

• [OgsyedIE] 对自我管理理念（每个人都是自己公司的CEO）持批评态度，认为这种想法会导致一切事物商品化，并将职场视为所有人对所有人的战争，这种思维最终会导致对人类关系的负面影响。

• [codeful] 基于十年工作经验分享了一种职场策略，建议在与新经理或团队合作时不要一开始就付出过多承诺和信任，而是等待团队面临第一次严重危机时再评估他们的真实能力。这种策略可以帮助更准确地判断同事在压力下的表现。

• [osigurdson] 对企业裁员和人工智能的趋势持不同看法，认为目前企业对人工智能取代人力的期待是过于自满的。他认为，企业如果不在当前竞争激烈的环境中充分利用AI+人力的组合优势，将会被竞争对手超越，因此现在并不是裁员的合适时机。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是自我管理理念（Self, Inc.）。[OgsyedIE] 认为这种理念会导致商品化一切，并加剧职场竞争和对立，而这种思维可能对职场文化产生负面影响。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是人工智能和裁员的关系。 [osigurdson] 认为企业依赖AI而不重视人力是短视的，当前竞争环境下更需要结合人力和AI的优势。
• 职场信任和承诺也是一个重要话题，[codeful] 通过自身经验提出了一种实际的职场生存策略，强调在危机中观察团队的真实能力，以避免过早付出过多信任。

这些观点共同构成了对现代职场中个人自由、企业策略以及职场关系的多元化讨论。

44362512.article_content:
June 2025
How To Care About Your Job When It Doesn't Care About You
We all want to do awesome things and make an impact at work. However, what we call “work” is a relationship between employer and employee that’s inherently and persistently designed to benefit the former over the latter. How do we meaningfully contribute, earn a living, and maybe even enjoy ourselves when the organization simply does not care about us?
It’s harsh, but that’s captialism, baby! Any organization (“org”) exists for a purpose that’s greater than the individuals within it (e.g., profit, public service). We are a means to that end. Same goes for anything we personally get out of the arrangement be it salary, experience, foosball tables, or free lunches.
This precarious and lopsided power dynamic manifests itself in our day-to-day in a variety of weird ways we often take for granted. Even if it never gets to something as extreme as layoffs or restructuring we still have to navigate this as best we can.
We need to do our best work possible all while one tiny fact looms in the back of our minds. At the end of the day
we’re just line items on somebody’s spreadsheet.
Hundreds Of People In A Trenchcoat
One prevailing assumption that crumbles under the slightest scrutiny is that an org is a cohesive entity. We all know deep down it’s merely a collective made up of people, and yet we overlook this all the time. Heaven help us all if the company refers to itself as family. Ugh!
Kevin Farzad
If an employer ever says “We’re like a family here” what they mean is they’re going to ruin you psychologically
The head of the collective—executive leadership—isn’t a single brain. It could be 3, 5, or 7 brains all trying to act like a cohesive unit. But if you personally had 7 brains inside your head how do you think you’d come across to others?
Companies are not rational actors
.
Anything an org does is just an emergent property of humans trying to work together. Organizations, especially large ones, are not optimizing for complete or perfect decisions. They’re optimizing for as much alignment and consensus as they can get to keep moving (sometimes by fiat).
By necessity these decisions will always be suboptimal and that will infuriate workers who care about what they do. Most of these decisions
will not make sense
because we can’t interpret a collective action as if it came from an individual. Rich Gilbert nails it in his great video
“Caring Less About Work can get us what we really want”
:
If you’re going to work and and you’re getting frustrated and you’re intelligent and you’re looking around at all the dummies around that are not making the right decision, that is by design.
We can plead, “How could they DO this?” or complain, “This is a dumb decision,” but executive leadership really is at arm’s length to us and our work. Leadership lacks the detail we regularly see in the course of our work and they’re dealing in the abstract. Actions from leadership will therefore often feel extreme, sudden, swift, half-baked, reactive, fickle, or temperamental.
The ultimate effect is that the org doesn’t care about us. One could even argue that it cannot care about us. An org is operating on another plane of reality entirely. Whatever it “does” says nothing about the individuals along for the ride. We’re better off not trying to interpret its actions too closely, lest we break our brains.
Corporate Dick Moves
Most of the time
Hanlon’s razor
explains the dysfunction we see, but the nature of orgs can also provide temptation or cover for some willful disregard and gaslighting.
A good example of gaslighting might be a lack of true upward mobility. Does the company promote often? Or does it say it will and then take forever to actually do it? How about raises—do they even happen and how are they calculated? Does the company promote from within or does it recruit a higher position with a new joiner?
That’s the carrot, but the stick is far worse! We’re always on the chopping block whether we know it or not. Not even management or the CTO are safe. Layoffs are ever-present and come in several forms.
If we’re unlucky enough to work somewhere that does
stack ranking
(e.g., Microsoft, Meta, Shopify) we can kinda sorta at least see it coming. Yay? Despite
all evidence
to the contrary
CEOs absolutely love this shit. They definitely do not care who’s let go and for those who remain—until the next quarter—they don’t care about the paranoia or distrust it causes.
Matt Boyd
When I interviewed at Meta, they had me do interviews with four engineers, seemingly chosen at random from within the company. The last guy had been there by far the longest. I asked him “What’s it like to work there?” and he said “Oh, working here will rewire your brain.”
Maybe stack ranking is too cumbersome… Probably best to just do layoffs arbitrarily. The company doesn’t even need to be in trouble!
Entirely profitable companies can do layoffs
, often more than once and with impunity. It’s a great fl

data.title: Comparison of Android-Based Operating Systems
data.author: Bluestein
data.article_summary: 这篇文章对比了几种基于AOSP的Android操作系统，包括GrapheneOS、CalyxOS、IodéOS、/e/、LineageOS和"Stock" Android。对比内容涵盖了它们是否为自由开源软件（FOSS）、是否去除了非必要代码（deblobbed）、网络控制、位置服务、系统范围的连接/追踪阻止、加密备份、多用户通知转发、紧急PIN、Android Auto和Google Pay兼容性、通话录音、截图功能、去谷歌化（连接Google的情况）、eSIM激活以及SUPL（辅助GNSS）提供者等方面。GrapheneOS和CalyxOS在隐私和安全方面功能较为强大，而"Stock" Android则较为依赖Google服务。各操作系统在功能和隐私保护上各有优劣。DivestOS原包含在对比中，但已于2024年底停止更新。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：GrapheneOS的优缺点及其与应用生态的兼容性

不同观点：
• [jajuuka] 认为该评论像是在吹捧GrapheneOS，因为文中的限定词都偏向于GrapheneOS，可能有失偏颇。
• [linuxandrew] 肯定GrapheneOS的表现，但批评其未预装F-Droid，且引导用户使用Google Play和Aurora。他指出F-Droid因其只提供FOSS（自由和开源软件）应用，在安全和隐私方面更有优势。虽然理解GrapheneOS兼容Google Play服务的实际需求，但他认为大多数懂行的用户会希望摆脱Google生态。
• [poulpy123] 关注GrapheneOS对设备的支持，指出目前只有Fairphone和Motorola设备得到广泛支持，而Google Pixel因停止发布特定源代码，可能无法长久获得支持。
• [sudahtigabulan] 指出即使不打算从原生Android切换到GrapheneOS，附录1中对各种隔离方案（如工作配置文件、私人空间、 secondary users）的比较对普通Android用户仍然有用。

补充讨论：
• GrapheneOS在应用生态上的选择成为争议焦点，尤其是对F-Droid和Google Play的不同立场。
• 设备支持也是讨论的重要方面，Fairphone和Motorola被认为是广泛支持的品牌，而Google Pixel的前景不被看好。
• 不同用户对是否需要完全摆脱Google生态有不同看法，反映出在隐私、安全和实用性之间的权衡。

Network controls for apps
The controls on LineageOS-based operating systems are leaky as their approach only disabled direct network access (socket) but doesn't disable indirect access via the INTERNET permission, which provides multiple ways of bypassing them not requiring collusion between apps. data.article_summary: 文章《"绿色"电动汽车的谎言：为什么你的特斯拉对环境的影响比你想象中更严重》揭示了特斯拉等电动汽车背后的环境代价。尽管特斯拉被宣传为环保选择，但其锂电池生产涉及大量锂、镍、钴等矿物的开采，导致水资源枯竭、生态破坏和碳排放。例如，智利的阿塔卡马盐湖矿区消耗大量水资源，印尼的镍矿开采破坏雨林。特斯拉承认其84%的碳足迹来自供应链，尤其是原材料开采。此外，锂电池回收率极低，预计到2030年将有1100万吨废旧电池，而回收过程本身也带来环境问题。文章质疑电动汽车是否真如宣传般环保，还是只是资源殖民主义的另一种形式。

The Big Lie Of ‘Green’ EVs: Why Your Tesla Is Worse For The Environment Than You Think
Philip Uwaoma

The Mineral Curse: How Your Tesla Replaced Oil Tyranny with Lithium Colonialism
The gleaming showrooms promise emission-free driving, the marketing touts a carbon-neutral future, and the sleek designs embody technological utopianism.
But beneath the polished veneer of your "green" Tesla lies a dirty secret: the electric vehicle revolution has merely swapped one extractive regime for another, creating fresh environmental catastrophes while laundering consumer consciences through the alchemy of carbon accounting. Is this salvation or resource colonialism rebranded for the climate age? You be the judge.
The Mining Mirage: When "Clean" Energy Ravages Landscapes
We're destroying the lungs of the planet to build "eco-friendly" transportation.
The lithium-ion battery powering your Model 3 or Model Y contains approximately 63 kg of lithium, extracted through processes that make oil drilling look surgical.
To be clear, most estimates suggest that a Tesla lithium-ion battery contains between 10 to 15 kg of lithium, depending on the battery chemistry and capacity. For example, a 75–82 kWh battery pack (common in Long Range and Performance trims) weighs around 450–500 kg in total, with lithium making up only a small fraction of that mass.
The rest includes aluminum, nickel, cobalt, graphite, and structural materials. The often-quoted “63 kg” figure refers to the amount of lithium carbonate equivalent (LCE) used in the production process, not the actual elemental lithium content. Since LCE is only about 18.8% lithium by weight, the real lithium content is much lower.
In Chile's Salar de Atacama, one of Earth's driest places, mining operations consume 65% of the region's scarce water reserves to produce a single ton of refined lithium.
To be clear, this figure refers to the overall water usage by mining operations in the area, not just the water required to produce a single ton of lithium. The process involves pumping mineral-rich brine from underground aquifers into large evaporation ponds, where water is lost to the atmosphere over months, concentrating the lithium.
Because the Salar is one of the driest places on Earth, with minimal rainfall and fragile ecosystems, this level of water extraction has raised serious concerns about sustainability, local agriculture, and indigenous communities. These indigenous communities watch as their ancestral lands become chemical sacrifice zones, where toxic evaporation ponds sprawl across 300 football fields of once-pristine desert .
Meanwhile in Indonesia, rainforests—the planet's critical carbon sinks—are clear-cut for nickel mining. Horizontal surface mining strips entire ecosystems to access ore deposits beneath topsoil.
The environmental calculus is grim: we're destroying the lungs of the planet to build "eco-friendly" transportation. Even Tesla's 2024 Impact Report admits that 84% of its carbon footprint comes from Scope 3 emissions, the largely unregulated upstream supply chain where this ecological devastation occurs.
To be clear, these emissions stem from indirect sources across Tesla’s value chain, primarily the upstream supply chain, including the extraction and processing of raw materials like lithium, nickel, and cobalt used in battery production.
While Scope 3 emissions are not directly produced by Tesla’s factories or vehicles (those fall under Scope 1 and 2), they represent the bulk of environmental impact due to the energy- and resource-intensive nature of mining, refining, and transporting materials.
This aligns with broader industry trends, where Scope 3 often accounts for the majority of emissions in manufacturing-heavy sectors. Tesla’s acknowledgment of this figure is part of a growing push for transparency, though critics argue that Scope 3 remains underregulated and difficult to mitigate without systemic supply chain reform.
The Recycling Myth: A Tsunami of Battery Waste Looms
Tesla boasts a 92% battery recycling rate at its Gigafactories, a statistic that obscures a brutal reality. This only applies to batteries they directly handle, representing a fraction of the coming waste tsunami.
Globally, less than 5% of lithium-ion batteries are recycled due to technical complexity and cost . With 11 million tonnes of EV batteries projected to be discarded by 2030, we're creating a time bomb of toxic waste .
The recycling process itself is environmentally dubious. Transporting batteries from Australia to European recycling facilities increases their global warming potential by 45%. And while lead-acid batteries achieve 90% recycling rates through standardized chemistry, lithium-ion batteries vary wildly in composition, making scalable soluti

data.title: Atuin – Magical Shell History
data.author: tosh
data.article_summary: Atuin 是一个开源工具，旨在通过同步、搜索和备份 shell 历史记录来提升用户的生产力。它支持跨多台设备同步历史记录，并采用端到端加密确保数据安全。Atuin 提供高效的搜索功能，允许用户根据主机、目录等条件进行过滤，还支持从多种格式导入现有历史数据。此外，它记录额外上下文信息，如工作目录和退出代码。安装过程简单，只需运行安装脚本并可选择注册云同步服务或自托管同步服务器。Atuin 适用于 Bash、ZSH、Fish 和 NuShell 等多种 shell。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Atuin 工具的使用体验、功能优势、隐私性、与不同 shell 的兼容性以及潜在的改进建议

不同观点：
• **支持并强烈推荐 Atuin**：
   - [nidnogg] 认为 Atuin 显著提升了他对命令历史的记忆和使用效率，尤其是在远程 SSH 会话中，极大提升了工作流速度，并表示会推荐给同事。
   - [MrSaints] 表示 Atuin 已经无缝融入日常工作流，极大提升了工作效率，并称其为一个坚实的开源项目。
   - [kenanfyi] 提到 Atuin 已经成为他每次设置新服务器时的必装软件，使用超过一年，体验非常好。

• **对同步功能的需求不一**：
   - [dmd] 表示自己不需要跨设备的同步功能，询问 Atuin 是否比现有的基于 fzf 的命令历史搜索 (C-r) 有显著优势。
   - [outcoldman] 分享了自己从 2017 年以来使用 SQLite 存储命令历史的经验，并开发了 ShellHistory 应用，支持 iCloud 同步。他认为 Atuin 和 ShellHistory 都是非常有价值的工具。

• **隐私与本地存储的替代方案**：
   - [moonshot5] 出于对数据不出设备的顾虑，开发了自己的工具 Raven，功能与 Atuin 类似，但不具备同步功能，且所有数据存储在本地 SQLite 数据库中。

• **与不同 shell 的兼容性讨论**：
   - [Tmpod] 询问 Atuin 在 fish shell 上的使用体验，并质疑其是否只是增加了同步功能，是否有必要使用。
   - [account-5] 提到 Atuin 可以与 Nushell 一起使用，虽然 Nushell 本身的历史搜索功能已经不错。

• **UI 与用户体验的改进建议**：
   - [picardo] 提到 Atuin 的搜索界面键绑定与传统命令历史使用习惯不一致，建议允许用户自定义键绑定，并认为不需要每次都展示全部历史记录。
   - [Despacito2019] 分享了自己将 Atuin 与 fzf 结合使用的自定义函数，并提供了代码示例，认为这样可以更好地适应自己的使用习惯。
   - [oliviergg] 建议开启配置中的 `workspaces = true` 选项，以限制历史记录在当前 Git 仓库范围内，提升搜索效率。

• **Atuin 的潜在问题与技术讨论**：
   - [tecleandor] 提到 Atuin 在 ZFS 文件系统上有已知的性能问题，并提供了相关文档和解决方案链接。
   - [pshirshov] 指出 Atuin 在搜索排序、终端清理和超时等方面存在一些问题，认为在某些方面 Atuin 比 fzf 有优势，但也有不足。

补充讨论：
• **与其他工具的对比**：
   - [Fervicus] 询问 Atuin 与 McFly 工具的比较，两者都是用于增强命令行历史搜索的工具。

• **长期用户的反馈**：
   - [nkko] 提到 Atuin 已经成为其配置文件安装脚本的一部分，使用两年以来，已经完全融入了其工作流，虽然几乎感受不到它的存在，但也证明了它的自然和高效。

争议焦点：
• 主要集中在 Atuin 的同步功能是否必要，以及不同用户对 UI 和键绑定的不同偏好。有些用户（如 [dmd]）不需要同步功能，而其他用户（如 [outcoldman]）则非常依赖同步功能。此外，用户对 Atuin 的默认键绑定和搜索界面的使用体验存在不同看法。

Shell history sync

Search decades of shell history, and recall it in an instant. Atuin offers configurable full text or fuzzy search, filterable by host, directory, etc.

Bring your existing history with you - Atuin supports importing from a wide variety of formats
Store extra context

FAQs
Frequently Asked Questions
Can you read my shell history?
No. Atuin is fully end-to-end encrypted. Without your key, nobody can see a thing. Read more about our encryption
here
!
Do I have to register?
If you would like to sync your shell history, registration is required. Otherwise, you can use Atuin locally as a fully-offline enhanced history search tool
What if I still don't trust your server?
If you would rather operate + maintain your own sync server then we have a guide
here
! Atuin supports self-hosting.
What technology does Atuin use?
Atuin is written in Rust, and stores your data in SQLite. Both technologies are known for being fast and reliable

Atuin currently supports Bash, ZSH, Fish and NuShell

主要讨论点：Atuin 工具的使用体验、功能优势、隐私性、与不同 shell 的兼容性以及潜在的改进建议

不同观点：
• **支持并强烈推荐 Atuin**：
   - [nidnogg] 认为 Atuin 显著提升了他对命令历史的记忆和使用效率，尤其是在远程 SSH 会话中，极大提升了工作流速度，并表示会推荐给同事。
   - [MrSaints] 表示 Atuin 已经无缝融入日常工作流，极大提升了工作效率，并称其为一个坚实的开源项目。
   - [kenanfyi] 提到 Atuin 已经成为他每次设置新服务器时的必装软件，使用超过一年，体验非常好。

• **对同步功能的需求不一**：
   - [dmd] 表示自己不需要跨设备的同步功能，询问 Atuin 是否比现有的基于 fzf 的命令历史搜索 (C-r) 有显著优势。
   - [outcoldman] 分享了自己从 2017 年以来使用 SQLite 存储命令历史的经验，并开发了 ShellHistory 应用，支持 iCloud 同步。他认为 Atuin 和 ShellHistory 都是非常有价值的工具。

• **隐私与本地存储的替代方案**：
   - [moonshot5] 出于对数据不出设备的顾虑，开发了自己的工具 Raven，功能与 Atuin 类似，但不具备同步功能，且所有数据存储在本地 SQLite 数据库中。

• **与不同 shell 的兼容性讨论**：
   - [Tmpod] 询问 Atuin 在 fish shell 上的使用体验，并质疑其是否只是增加了同步功能，是否有必要使用。
   - [account-5] 提到 Atuin 可以与 Nushell 一起使用，虽然 Nushell 本身的历史搜索功能已经不错。

• **UI 与用户体验的改进建议**：
   - [picardo] 提到 Atuin 的搜索界面键绑定与传统命令历史使用习惯不一致，建议允许用户自定义键绑定，并认为不需要每次都展示全部历史记录。
   - [Despacito2019] 分享了自己将 Atuin 与 fzf 结合使用的自定义函数，并提供了代码示例，认为这样可以更好地适应自己的使用习惯。
   - [oliviergg] 建议开启配置中的 `workspaces = true` 选项，以限制历史记录在当前 Git 仓库范围内，提升搜索效率。

• **Atuin 的潜在问题与技术讨论**：
   - [tecleandor] 提到 Atuin 在 ZFS 文件系统上有已知的性能问题，并提供了相关文档和解决方案链接。
   - [pshirshov] 指出 Atuin 在搜索排序、终端清理和超时等方面存在一些问题，认为在某些方面 Atuin 比 fzf 有优势，但也有不足。

补充讨论：
• **与其他工具的对比**：
   - [Fervicus] 询问 Atuin 与 McFly 工具的比较，两者都是用于增强命令行历史搜索的工具。

• **长期用户的反馈**：
   - [nkko] 提到 Atuin 已经成为其配置文件安装脚本的一部分，使用两年以来，已经完全融入了其工作流，虽然几乎感受不到它的存在，但也证明了它的自然和高效。

争议焦点：
• 主要集中在 Atuin 的同步功能是否必要，以及不同用户对 UI 和键绑定的不同偏好。有些用户（如 [dmd]）不需要同步功能，而其他用户（如 [outcoldman]）则非常依赖同步功能。此外，用户对 Atuin 的默认键绑定和搜索界面的使用体验存在不同看法。

data.title: Google could be forced to change UK search as watchdog takes steps
data.author: chrisjj
data.article_summary: 英国竞争与市场管理局（CMA）计划根据《数字市场、竞争与消费者法案》将谷歌认定为具有“战略市场地位”的公司，可能强制其对搜索业务进行调整。这包括为用户提供选择其他搜索服务的选项，确保搜索结果排名公平，以及让出版商对内容使用有更多控制权。CMA还将考虑进一步措施，如增加搜索广告透明度，但承认这些可能更复杂。谷歌在英国搜索市场占90%以上份额，若CMA在10月确认决定，谷歌将成为新法规下首个被指定的公司。CMA首席执行官Sarah Cardell表示，这些措施将为企业和消费者提供更多选择和控制，并促进创新。部分措施可能延迟至2026年实施，如对默认搜索引擎协议的处理将待美国司法部与谷歌的诉讼结束后再决定。

Google is likely to be the first company designated by the CMA under the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act.

Google could be forced to change UK search as watchdog takes steps
CMA proposes tightening regulation, which could lead to site giving users option to choose alternative services
Business live – latest updates
Dan Milmo
Global technology editor
Tue 24 Jun 2025 08.21 EDT
First published on Tue 24 Jun 2025 02.44 EDT
Share
Google could be forced to make a series of changes to its search business, including giving internet users an option to choose alternative services, after the UK competition watchdog proposed to tighten regulation of the company.
The Competition and Market Authority (CMA) is preparing to designate the world’s largest search engine with “strategic market status” – a term that gives the watchdog extra powers to regulate technology companies deemed to have considerable market heft.
Google, which is owned by the US tech group
Alphabet
, accounts for more than 90% of search queries in Britain.
The CMA said it was minded to introduce bespoke regulatory measures for Google, including giving users “choice screens” to help them switch between search services, ensuring fair ranking of search results, and providing more control for publishers over how their content is used, including in AI-generated responses.
Google battling fox incursion on roof of £1bn London office
Read more
If the CMA confirms its decision in October, Google will be the first company designated since the regulator
gained new powers this year
. The CMA will then consult on the first wave of bespoke measures.
One option for the choice screens would be to include new AI-powered rivals in the search space, such as Perplexity and ChatGPT.
The CMA will also consider further action on other issues such as introducing more transparency into Google’s search advertising business. However, the CMA struck a note of caution on this second wave of potential measures, saying interventions in these areas “may be more complex to develop”.
Sarah Cardell, the CMA chief executive, said the announcement marked an important milestone in a new regulatory regime under the recent Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act.
Cardell said: “These targeted and proportionate actions would give UK businesses and consumers more choice and control over how they interact with Google’s search services – as well as unlocking greater opportunities for innovation across the UK tech sector and broader economy.”
The CMA said it planned further action to address more complex issues over a longer period, starting in 2026, such as concerns about Google’s treatment of rival specialised search platforms and transparency and control in search advertising.
The watchdog is also delaying action on “default agreements” where Google pays to be the search engine of choice on products such as the Apple iPhone until the conclusion of a court case between the company and the US department of justice – which is
seeking to end such arrangements
.
The CMA also announced that it would delay a third strategic market status designation until next year. A verdict on designating Apple and Google’s smartphone platforms as worthy of the status is expected next month.
Tom Smith, a competition lawyer at the UK law firm Geradin Partners and the CMA’s former legal director, said the regulator could have gone “harder and faster” on Google but was trying to avoid any accusation that it was anti-growth. The chancellor, Rachel Reeves, has ordered regulators to
do more to encourage economic growth
.

Smith said the CMA was proposing a range of sensible measures that would encourage growth and benefit businesses and consumers.
Referring to the second wave of potential measures – such as paying for content from news publishers or helping specialised search engines such as for travel sites – he added: “It is, however, disappointing that some key measures that would benefit the news industry and local search providers have been delayed to next year. The CMA could have gone harder and faster, but it is treading carefully to avoid being labelled as being ‘anti-growth’ by Google and its allies.”

data.author: asix66
data.article_summary: 本文简要介绍了与YouTube及相关服务的一些重要信息。内容包括关于YouTube的介绍、新闻发布、版权声明、联系方式、创作者信息、广告、开发者条款、隐私政策、安全政策以及YouTube的使用方式和新型功能测试。此外，还提及了NFL Sunday Ticket服务和版权归属为2025年的Google LLC。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：基拉韦厄火山（Kilauea）的活动情况及其影响

不同观点：
• **asix66** 提供了有关基拉韦厄火山活动的实时视频链接和美国地质调查局（USGS）的更新信息，试图为讨论提供事实依据和官方资源。
• **jmward01** 认为火山的喷发是定期发生的，并引用了Geology Hub对之前喷发事件的报道视频，暗示此类事件具有一定的规律性。
• **jasonthorsness** 推荐乘坐直升机观赏基拉韦厄火山，强调即使火山未喷发，冷却的熔岩流路径依然壮观，显示出火山的巨大影响力。
• **dluan** 关注火山喷发对空气质量的影响，尤其是VOG（火山烟雾）问题，表达了对风向变化的担忧，因为这可能加剧空气污染。
• **1970-01-01** 对实时视频链接的价值提出质疑，认为视频中只能看到蒸汽，没有实质性的喷发活动。
• **dboreham** 以幽默的方式提到自己似乎与火山喷发“相克”，并开玩笑说如果有人希望火山停止喷发，可以送机票让他去现场。
• **Eduard** 对视频中的某个时间点提出具体要求，希望看到“熔岩高达1000英尺”的片段。

补充讨论：
• **ganeshkrishnan** 分享了关于大岛（Big Island）地理和气候多样性的个人体验，强调该地区从沙漠到雪山再到热带等多种气候带的独特性，并描述了一次特别的公共汽车旅行经历。

争议焦点：
• 实时视频的价值：asix66提供的实时视频链接被1970-01-01认为没有实际内容，这显示出对信息实用性的不同期望。
• 火山喷发对生活的影响：dluan对VOG问题的担忧与其他讨论者对火山喷发壮观景象的欣赏形成对比，显示出不同人群对火山活动的不同关注点。

总结：讨论主要围绕基拉韦厄火山的活动情况、观赏建议及其对环境和生活的影响展开，参与者提供了多种信息来源和个人体验，展现了对该火山活动的多样化视角。

data.title: Timdle – Place historical events in chronological order
data.author: maskinberg
data.article_summary: TIMDLE是一个类似于每日猜词游戏的在线平台。玩家可以参与每天的 timeline 猜谜，通过推测一系列事件的正确时间线来完成游戏。玩家还可以创建自己的游戏，自定义时间线供他人猜测。如有任何问题或反馈，玩家可以通过daily.timdle@gmail.com联系平台。游戏简单有趣，适合喜欢历史事件和时间线的玩家。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对TIMDLE游戏的体验和相关问题的讨论，包括游戏机制、用户界面、类似游戏的比较以及可能的商业化。

不同观点：
• [正面评价] 
  - [neuronflux] 享受游戏，特别是女朋友对得分和表情符号的有趣反应。
  - [alkh] 分享了自己的高分成绩，表示对游戏的喜爱。
  - [maskinberg] 也分享了自己的高分，显示对游戏的参与度。

• [对命名和游戏形式的调侃]
  - [NoboruWataya] 认为在Wordle之后的四年，类似命名的游戏应该有所创新，而不是继续使用"-le"后缀。同时提到游戏中事件可能导致的混淆，质疑游戏的智能性。

• [用户界面问题]
  - [zdc1] 提到游戏窗口调整导致的事件隐藏问题，强调可见滚动条的必要性。

• [商业化潜力]
  - [etewiah] 提出如果游戏变得非常流行，是否有可能实现商业化。

• [游戏灵感来源]
  - [pmontra] 提到游戏可能受到2022年桌游"Trekking Through History"的启发，并提供了相关链接。

• [与其他游戏的比较]
  - [nonethewiser] 指出TIMDLE类似于非常简单的游戏"Timeline"，并提供了相关链接。
  - [mrgoldenbrown] 认为TIMDLE像是电子版的桌游Chronology，并提到其作为派对游戏的优点，提供了相关链接。
  - [xnx] 更喜欢TIMDLE的左右时间线，而不是纽约时报的从下到上的时间线。

• [游戏改进建议]
  - [wavemode] 提出对游戏评分的改进建议，希望可以按正确顺序排列所有事件并根据尝试次数评分。

• [游戏体验问题]
  - [stuartjohnson12] 提到初始提示令人困惑，导致错误选择，认为可能是个人技能问题，但分享了困惑的体验。

• [技术问题]
  - [Artoooooor] 遇到技术问题，显示“出了问题，请稍后再试”，并幽默地指出两个事件已经按时间顺序排列。

补充讨论：
• 一些用户分享了自己的游戏成绩和策略，如alkh和maskinberg。
• 对游戏机制的改进建议，如wavemode的评分系统建议。
• 技术问题和用户界面问题，如zdc1的窗口调整问题和Artooooor的技术故障。
• 游戏的潜在灵感和类似游戏的比较，如pmontra和nonethewiser的讨论。

data.author: ibobev
data.article_summary: 这篇文章简要介绍了GPU的基本工作原理和性能优化策略，特别关注NVIDIA A100 GPU的架构。GPU的特点是计算速度远超内存访问速度，A100每秒可执行19.5万亿次浮点运算（TFLOPS），但内存带宽仅为1.5 TB/s。GPU通过多层内存和计算层次结构来缓解这一瓶颈，包括全局内存（VRAM）、流多处理器（SM）、共享内存（SRAM）和寄存器。线程是执行的最小单位，被硬件分为每组32个的"Warp"进行同步执行。文章还讨论了两种提升性能的策略：融合（Operator Fusion）和分块（Tiling），以及如何通过增加算术强度和隐藏延迟来进一步优化性能。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：GPU在运行机器学习模型时的性能优化问题及其相关架构分析

不同观点：
• [b0a04gl] 分享了在使用llama.cpp和vllm时遇到的性能问题，特别是在批量处理提示词时，llama.cpp出现延迟，而vllm表现更好。经过分析发现，这是由于内存布局问题，导致GPU的缓存访问效率低下。通过调整内存布局，取得了2倍的速度提升。该用户还提出希望找到更简便的方式进行类似实验，而不需要耗费大量时间进行试错。

• [elashri] 认为文章标题具有一定误导性，因为文章讨论的内容主要围绕NVIDIA的GPU架构，而不同厂商（如AMD）的GPU在算术强度和带宽上的平衡点不同。例如，AMD的Instinct MI300具有更高的算术强度和更大的内存带宽，这与NVIDIA的GPU有显著差异。此外，AMD的GPU不支持CUDA，这既是优点也是缺点。

• [LarsDu88] 强调文章内容主要适用于现代NVIDIA的GPU，而不一定适用于所有GPU，尤其是早期（如2003年）的GPU，它们主要针对游戏渲染管道设计，与现代通用计算的GPU有很大区别。

争议焦点：
• 不同GPU架构（如NVIDIA和AMD）在处理机器学习任务时的性能差异以及内存布局对性能的影响。

44365320.article_content:
Basic facts about GPUs
last updated:
2025-06-18
I’ve been trying to get a better sense of how GPUs work. I’ve read a lot online, but the following posts were particularly helpful:
Making Deep Learning Go Brrrr From First Principles
What Shapes Do Matrix Multiplications Like?
How to Optimize a CUDA Matmul Kernel for cuBLAS-like Performance: a Worklog
This post collects various facts I learned from these resources.
Acknowledgements: Thanks to
Alex McKinney
for comments on
independent thread scheduling
.
Table of Contents
Compute and memory hierarchy
Two Performance Regimes: Memory-Bound and Compute-Bound
The Third Regime: Overhead
Two basic strategies for increasing performance: Fusion and Tiling
Operator Fusion
Tiling: Strategy for Compute-Bound Kernels
The Coalesced Load: HBM to SRAM
Synchronization
The On-Chip Hardware: Banks and Warps
The Bank Conflict Problem
The On-Chip Compute Phase: Increasing Arithmetic Intensity
Additional Performance Considerations
Occupancy and Latency Hiding
Avoiding Thread Divergence
Quantization
Compute and memory hierarchy
A GPU’s design creates an imbalance since it can compute much faster than it can access its main memory. An NVIDIA A100 GPU, for example, can perform 19.5 trillion 32-bit floating-point operations per second (TFLOPS), but its memory bandwidth is only about 1.5 terabytes per second (TB/s). In the time it takes to read a single 4-byte number, the GPU could have performed over 50 calculations.
Below is a diagram of the compute and memory hierarchy for an NVIDIA A100 GPU. The numbers I quote for flops/s and TB/s are exclusive to A100s.
+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                               Global Memory (VRAM)                              |
|                            (~40 GB, ~1.5 TB/s on A100)                          |
+----------------------------------------+----------------------------------------+
| (Slow off-chip bus)
+----------------------------------------v----------------------------------------+
|                            Streaming Multiprocessor (SM)                        |
|                     (1 of 108 SMs on an A100, each ~(19.5/108) TFLOPS)          |
|                           (2048 threads, 64 warps, 32 blocks)                   |
| +-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+ |
| |                        Shared Memory (SRAM) / L1 Cache                        |
| |                    (~192 KB on-chip workbench, 19.5 TB/s)                     |
| +-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+ |
| |                        Register File (~256 KB, ? TB/s)                        |
| +-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+ |
| |                                                                             | |
| |                //-- A "Block" of threads runs on one SM --//                | |
| | +--------------------------+ +------------------------+                     | |
| | |      Warp 0 (32 thr)     | |      Warp 1 (32 thr)   | ... (up to 32 warps)| |
| | | +----------------------+ | +----------------------+ |                     | |
| | | | Thread 0 Registers   | | | Thread 32 Registers  | |                     | |
| | | | [reg0: float]        | | | [reg0: float]        | |                     | |
| | | | [reg1: float] ...    | | | [reg1: float] ...    | |                     | |
| | | +----------------------+ | +----------------------+ |                     | |
| | +--------------------------+ +------------------------+                     | |
| |                                                                             | |
+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
This diagram shows the performance hierarchy.
1
Global Memory (VRAM)
is the large, slow, off-chip memory pool where all data initially lives. A
Streaming Multiprocessor (SM)
is the GPU’s unit of computation. To work, it must fetch data over the slow bus. To mitigate this, each SM has fast, on-chip
Shared Memory
(SRAM) with a bandwidth of 19.5 TB/s.
2
Programmers use this as a manually-managed cache.
A
thread
is the smallest unit of execution. Each thread has a private set of
Registers
to hold values for immediate computation, with access speeds over ?? TB/s.
3
The hardware groups threads into
Warps
of 32. This post analyzes performance using the simplified model of
lockstep execution
, where all 32 threads in a warp execute the same instruction at the same time.
4
On an A100, an SM has an upper limit of 64 warps. A programmer groups threads into a
Block
, a grid of threads that is guaranteed to run on a single SM. A block can be one, two, or three-dimensional. For simplicity, this post will focus on square two-dimensional blocks of
BLOCK_DIM x BLOCK_DIM
threads, where the total number of threads cannot exceed the hardware limit of 1024. All threads in a block share ac

data.title: Finding a 27-year-old easter egg in the Power Mac G3 ROM
data.author: zdw
data.article_summary: 作者Doug Brown在探索Power Mac G3 ROM时，意外发现了一个隐藏了27年的彩蛋。通过使用工具Hex Fiend和Eric Harmon的Mac ROM模板，作者在ROM中发现了一个包含团队照片的资源（类型为HPOE），但如何显示该照片一直是个谜。作者进一步分析nitt资源ID 43时，发现了“secret ROM image”等字符串，推测与彩蛋相关。经过深入分析和使用Ghidra反编译工具，作者确认了该字符串与.EDisk驱动和SCSI Manager有关，并猜测存在一种类似于早期PowerPC Mac的方法来显示该图片，但具体操作未被记录。作者最终通过反汇编获得更多线索，但未能完全解锁显示方法。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于早期电脑中的彩蛋（Easter Eggs）及其背后的人文意义，以及现代产品设计中彩蛋的消失和可能原因。

不同观点：
• Waterluvian：彩蛋给人一种早期桌面PC时代的感觉，能够让人感受到背后有真实的团队在工作。然而，现在的“产品人”更希望控制产品的整体形象，倾向于去人性化，以避免潜在风险。Waterluvian设想如果现代iPhone中有类似的彩蛋，展示随机开发者，但认为这可能会冒犯高层的品味。

• tasty_freeze：提到其以前同事在80到90年代为苹果工作，硬件团队在设计和调试中付出了巨大努力，但软件团队却通过彩蛋独占荣誉，忽略了硬件团队的贡献，令其不满。

• RomanPushkin：认为彩蛋展示了企业背后真实的人，并对比了像扎克伯格这样的富豪常自称独立完成某项成就，而真正的贡献者却默默无闻。同时指出，像乔布斯这样的人可能会禁止这种做法。

• postexitus：提到“We made the Amiga, they f----d it up!”这样的历史信息，暗示团队内部的矛盾和不满。

• RainyDayTmrw：对早期计算机团队规模小而高效表示赞赏，并希望能够回归那种状态。

• chrisbrandow：提到曾有人在iPad上发现彩蛋，通过Playground应用可以调出旧版的ROM logo，但之后难以找到相关资料。

• spaceisballer：回忆90年代在图书馆阅读MacWorld杂志，并通过特定操作在Apple IIci中解锁某些内容。

• burnt-resistor：非常怀念彩蛋，希望它们能回归。

• jan_Sate：对逆向工程发现彩蛋的过程表示兴趣，并询问如何学习逆向工程的建议。

• iosjunkie：认为这可以成为“难倒专家”节目的好素材，表达了对过去时光的怀念。

• wk_end：提到乔布斯在1997年 reportedly 禁止彩蛋，认为乔布斯的回归虽然对苹果是净收益，但公司文化和身份却因此失去了某些东西。

• tambourine_man：认为旧机器激发了彩蛋的创造和发现，并怀疑未来是否还有人会在MacBook Air的EFI中挖掘出类似的东西。

• perdomon：尝试使用Infinite Mac浏览器工具重现彩蛋未果，但仍认为这是一个很酷的发现，并质疑现代苹果是否还敢加入这种有趣的内容。

• MortyWaves：对彩蛋中未完全读取的字符串感到困惑，试图理解其含义。

• ryeguy_24：惊叹于人们如何发现这些彩蛋，认为这是人类集体探索知识的体现，并表达了对科学探索精神的赞赏。

补充讨论：
• 彩蛋的发现和逆向工程的难度：如jan_Sate和perdomon提到的，逆向工程发现彩蛋的过程非常复杂，且难以重现。
• 彩蛋背后的人文意义：如Waterluvian、RomanPushkin和wk_end提到的，彩蛋展示了产品背后真实的人和团队的努力，具有重要的人文价值。
• 现代产品设计中彩蛋的消失：如burnt-resistor、wk_end和tambourine_man提到的，现代产品设计中彩蛋逐渐消失，可能与企业控制产品形象和乔布斯的影响有关。

争议焦点：
• 彩蛋的价值和现代产品设计的取舍：一些人怀念和赞赏彩蛋的人文意义，而另一些人如乔布斯的做法，则认为应该去人性化以保持产品形象的专业性和一致性。

Finding a 27-year-old easter egg in the Power Mac G3 ROM
Doug Brown
Classic Mac
,
Reverse engineering
2025-06-24
I was recently poking around inside the original Power Macintosh G3’s ROM and accidentally discovered an easter egg that nobody has documented until now.
This story starts with me on a lazy Sunday using
Hex Fiend
in conjunction with
Eric Harmon’s Mac ROM template (ROM Fiend)
to look through the resources stored in the Power Mac G3’s ROM. This ROM was used in the beige desktop, minitower, and all-in-one G3 models from 1997 through 1999.
As I write this post in mid-2025, I’m having a really difficult time accepting the fact that the Power Mac G3 is now over 27 years old. Wow!
While I was browsing through the ROM, two things caught my eye:
First, there was a resource of type
HPOE
which contained a JPEG image of a bunch of people, presumably people who worked on these Mac models.
This wasn’t anything new;
Pierre Dandumont wrote about it back in 2014
. However, in his post, he mentioned that he hadn’t figured out how to display this particular hidden image on the actual machine. Several older Macs have secret keypress combinations to show similar pictures, but the mechanism for displaying this one was a complete mystery.
The second thing I found was a big clue: I kept looking for other interesting information in the ROM, and eventually I stumbled upon
nitt
resource ID 43, named “Native 4.3”. Thanks to
Keith Kaisershot’s earlier Pippin research
, I was quickly able to conclude that this was the PowerPC-native SCSI Manager 4.3 code. The SCSI Manager wasn’t what piqued my interest about this resource though. At the very end of the data, I found some interesting Pascal strings:
These strings were definitely intriguing:
.Edisk
secret ROM image
The Team
The “secret ROM image” text in particular seemed like it could be related to the picture shown above. I decided to dive deeper to see if I could figure out why the SCSI Manager contained these strings, in the hopes that I could solve the mystery. Would this be the clue I needed in order to figure out how to instruct the Power Mac G3 to display this picture?
Some quick Internet searching for the phrase “secret ROM image” revealed that
it had been used for easter eggs with earlier PowerPC Macs
. On those machines, you just had to type the text, select it, and drag it to the desktop. Then, the picture would appear. That approach didn’t work on the G3.
I suspected there was some similar way to access this hidden image, but nobody had documented it, at least not as far as I could find. So I had no choice but to disassemble the code and see where this text was used. What is it with me and all these crazy rabbit holes?
I extracted the entire
nitt
resource ID 43 to a file and inspected it:
$ file nitt43
nitt43: header for PowerPC PEF executable
That wasn’t too surprising, considering that the first twelve bytes were “Joy!peffpwpc”. I fed this entire file into
Ghidra
, which immediately recognized it as a PEF file and had no trouble loading it. Although I’m pretty familiar with reading x86 and ARM assembly, I know essentially nothing about PowerPC assembly code. Thankfully, Ghidra’s decompiler worked very well with this file.
There was one problem, though: it didn’t detect any references to the “secret ROM image” string, other than inside of a huge list of pointers to variables. After scratching my head a little bit, I realized that Ghidra wasn’t doing a great job of finding references to several variables. Luckily, running Auto Analyze a second time after the initial analysis seemed to help it find several more references to things, including all of the strings I was interested in! I didn’t change any options with the analyzer; it just found more stuff on the second run.
The function that used all of these strings was definitely doing something with the .EDisk driver, which I already knew was the RAM disk driver because of past hackery. It seemed to be using
strncmp()
to see if a string was equal to “secret ROM image”, and if so, it would create/open/write a file named “The Team”.
I cleaned up this decompilation quite a bit by giving names to variables and figuring out data types. Fortunately, a lot of the functions like
PBGetVInfoSync()
had lots of public documentation, so I just had to tell Ghidra about the various Mac Toolbox structs being used.
Okay, that’s a lot easier to understand!
I couldn’t figure out how to format the 32-bit function arguments such as 0x48504f45 into four-letter codes like
HPOE
, so that’s what the comments are. Ghidra simply wouldn’t let me display them as ASCII in the decompilation no matter what I did, even though hovering over the constant showed a tooltip with the equivalent text. This is easy to do in IDA, but I couldn’t figure out how to convince Ghidra to do it. I tried Set Equate, but it d
44365806.article_summary: 作者Doug Brown在探索Power Mac G3 ROM时，意外发现了一个隐藏了27年的彩蛋。通过使用工具Hex Fiend和Eric Harmon的Mac ROM模板，作者在ROM中发现了一个包含团队照片的资源（类型为HPOE），但如何显示该照片一直是个谜。作者进一步分析nitt资源ID 43时，发现了“secret ROM image”等字符串，推测与彩蛋相关。经过深入分析和使用Ghidra反编译工具，作者确认了该字符串与.EDisk驱动和SCSI Manager有关，并猜测存在一种类似于早期PowerPC Mac的方法来显示该图片，但具体操作未被记录。作者最终通过反汇编获得更多线索，但未能完全解锁显示方法。

主要讨论点：关于早期电脑中的彩蛋（Easter Eggs）及其背后的人文意义，以及现代产品设计中彩蛋的消失和可能原因。

不同观点：
• Waterluvian：彩蛋给人一种早期桌面PC时代的感觉，能够让人感受到背后有真实的团队在工作。然而，现在的“产品人”更希望控制产品的整体形象，倾向于去人性化，以避免潜在风险。Waterluvian设想如果现代iPhone中有类似的彩蛋，展示随机开发者，但认为这可能会冒犯高层的品味。

• tasty_freeze：提到其以前同事在80到90年代为苹果工作，硬件团队在设计和调试中付出了巨大努力，但软件团队却通过彩蛋独占荣誉，忽略了硬件团队的贡献，令其不满。

• RomanPushkin：认为彩蛋展示了企业背后真实的人，并对比了像扎克伯格这样的富豪常自称独立完成某项成就，而真正的贡献者却默默无闻。同时指出，像乔布斯这样的人可能会禁止这种做法。

• postexitus：提到“We made the Amiga, they f----d it up!”这样的历史信息，暗示团队内部的矛盾和不满。

• RainyDayTmrw：对早期计算机团队规模小而高效表示赞赏，并希望能够回归那种状态。

• chrisbrandow：提到曾有人在iPad上发现彩蛋，通过Playground应用可以调出旧版的ROM logo，但之后难以找到相关资料。

• spaceisballer：回忆90年代在图书馆阅读MacWorld杂志，并通过特定操作在Apple IIci中解锁某些内容。

• burnt-resistor：非常怀念彩蛋，希望它们能回归。

• jan_Sate：对逆向工程发现彩蛋的过程表示兴趣，并询问如何学习逆向工程的建议。

• iosjunkie：认为这可以成为“难倒专家”节目的好素材，表达了对过去时光的怀念。

• wk_end：提到乔布斯在1997年 reportedly 禁止彩蛋，认为乔布斯的回归虽然对苹果是净收益，但公司文化和身份却因此失去了某些东西。

• tambourine_man：认为旧机器激发了彩蛋的创造和发现，并怀疑未来是否还有人会在MacBook Air的EFI中挖掘出类似的东西。

• perdomon：尝试使用Infinite Mac浏览器工具重现彩蛋未果，但仍认为这是一个很酷的发现，并质疑现代苹果是否还敢加入这种有趣的内容。

• MortyWaves：对彩蛋中未完全读取的字符串感到困惑，试图理解其含义。

• ryeguy_24：惊叹于人们如何发现这些彩蛋，认为这是人类集体探索知识的体现，并表达了对科学探索精神的赞赏。

• 彩蛋背后的人文意义：如Waterluvian、RomanPushkin和wk_end提到的，彩蛋展示了产品背后真实的人和团队的努力，具有重要的人文价值。
• 现代产品设计中彩蛋的消失：如burnt-resistor、wk_end和tambourine_man提到的，现代产品设计中彩蛋逐渐消失，可能与企业控制产品形象和乔布斯的影响有关。

• 彩蛋的价值和现代产品设计的取舍：一些人怀念和赞赏彩蛋的人文意义，而另一些人如乔布斯的做法，则认为应该去人性化以保持产品形象的专业性和一致性。

data.title: Show HN: Oasis – an open-source, 3D-printed smart terrarium
data.author: jbuch
data.article_summary: Oasis是一个开源的智能生态缸项目，大部分部件可通过3D打印制作。它专为喜湿植物如苔藓、蕨类、兰花等设计，具备高功率LED灯、喷雾器、风扇、温湿度传感器等组件，并支持通过WiFi进行远程控制。项目包含使用CadQuery设计的CAD模型、KiCad设计的电子电路以及用Rust编写的软件。虽然电子部分较为复杂，但可通过JLCPCB等公司订购预制件，或自行焊接组装。未来可能推出组装套件，感兴趣者可填写表单订阅更新。项目详情见[Oasis官网](https://oasis-terrarium.com)。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：该项目的评价与改进建议

不同观点：
• craghack对项目中的电子元件保护提出建议，特别是对超声波加湿器和热传感器的保护措施。他建议通过更换电容或将传感器独立放置来避免问题。
• Aurornis对新手如何选择适合的植物表示关注，并请求提供相关学习资源和购买渠道的链接。

• yreg建议在项目介绍页面增加默认尺寸的说明，以便更好地了解成品规格。
• dwroberts对项目中的加湿设备表示赞赏，并提出水体消毒的建议，提到使用UVC灯进行消毒，同时提醒注意安全问题。
• mandsgoo和senectus1对项目表示赞赏和个人兴趣，但没有提出具体建议或意见。

• bethekidyouwant对项目的材料构成提出看法，指出该项目并非主要使用3D打印材料。

补充讨论：
• 评论中涉及多个技术细节的讨论，如电容更换、热传感器设计、UVC LED应用等，显示出评论者对项目技术深度的关注。
• 对植物选择和照明方案的讨论反映了新手用户在实际操作中可能面临的困惑和需求。

• 总体上，评论者对项目的创新性和实用性表示肯定，但也提出了多个改进建议和实际应用中的考虑因素。

Oasis
https://oasis-terrarium.com
Oasis is a fully open-source, mostly 3d-printed smart terrarium. It provides the ideal environment for humidity-loving plants like mosses, ferns, orchids, and many others. The design includes:
high power LED lighting
a mister for providing plants with water and maintaining high humidity
fans for airflow
a temperature/humidity sensor for monitoring environment conditions
wifi connectivity to allow control and configuration from your phone or computer (see
web interface
)
See the website for pictures, build details and more:
https://oasis-terrarium.com
.
This repository contains full sources for the CAD models (designed with
CadQuery
), electronics (designed in
KiCad
), and software (written in rust using the
esp-rs
libraries).
Most of this project is accessible to the average DIYer with access to a 3d printer, however the electronics portion of the project is a bit more involved. Fully-assembled electronics can be ordered from companies like JLCPCB by uploading the files from this repo, but this can be expensive for small order quantities. Those with the right equipment and experience soldering small parts could order the bare PCBs and components separately, then do their own assembly and soldering.
I'd like to eventually offer the assembled electronics as a kit, but don't have immediate plans for doing so. To express interest in a kit and to subscribe for future updates, please fill out this form:
https://forms.gle/WesLJEf8hVrUT4jXA
.

data.title: PlasticList – Plastic Levels in Foods
data.author: homebrewer
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：塑料对食品的潜在影响及健康风险

不同观点：
• **反对使用塑料研磨器**：dredmorbius认为塑料研磨器会随着使用将塑料磨入食物中，且这种设计不应存在。他引用了Stackexchange上的讨论支持自己的观点，并提供了在Walmart上搜索塑料研磨器的结果作为例子。
  
• **支持众筹测试特定产品**：cjflog支持通过众筹方式测试具体产品中的塑料化学物质，认为这种方式可以推动供应链的清洁化，并提到了PlasticList和laboratory.love作为参考。

• **质疑塑料来源**：eestrada对“农场玻璃瓶装生牛奶”中仍含有塑料表示担忧，并质疑是否由于使用含有塑料的挤奶机管道导致。

• **历史产品中的DEHP**：dmm对1920年代产品中发现DEHP感到困惑，因为这种化学物质在1930年代才被合成，并提供了具体产品链接作为例子。

• **对DEHP和DEHT安全限量的讨论**：showerst分析了DEHP和DEHT的安全限量，认为即使主要食用RXBars和Sweetgreen等食品，摄入量仍在安全限量内，但同时也表达了对限量标准的可能过高的担忧。

• **塑料关注度与实际风险的对比**：xnx认为塑料对食品的影响受到过多关注，而如糖分和酒精消费等已确认的健康风险却未得到同等重视，并引用了关于BPA/BPS的报道作为例子。

• **具体食品中的塑料含量**：aydyn指出星巴克拿铁中含有大量塑料，并提供了具体产品链接。

• **对草饲牛排的讽刺**：cheeseomlit讽刺了Whole Foods草饲牛排中含有塑料的可能性。

• **消费者应对措施的建议**：ls-a和zkmon都提出了消费者应如何应对塑料污染的问题，zkmon特别询问了塑料对消化系统外的影响及可能的补救措施。

• **历史产品对比**：egberts1和chiffre01都提到了历史产品的对比，egberts1惊讶于朝鲜战争时期的糖定量与现代商店购买的糖的对比，chiffre01则具体比较了1952年朝鲜战争口粮和Whole Foods的无骨草饲牛排。

补充讨论：
• **对不同单位换算的困惑**：metalrain对讨论中使用的不同单位表示困惑，认为这一领域仍处于早期阶段。
  
• **对水源中PFAS的关注**：johncole指出PFAS是比食品中塑料更危险的物质，并建议通过蒸馏水去除PFAS及其他有害物质，提供了相关链接支持其观点。

data.title: Circular Microcomputers embedded and powered by repurposed smartphone components
data.author: Bluestein
data.article_summary: Citronics推出全球首款循环微型计算机，利用翻新的智能手机组件打造，具备4G LTE、WiFi、以太网等连接方式，采用多核CPU和GPU，运行基于Linux的操作系统。产品可从1台扩展至10,000台，支持开发和定制，适用于物联网、边缘计算、自动化等领域。公司提供从云管理到工程支持的全方位服务，帮助加速产品上市并优化成本。其解决方案强调可持续性和成本效益，通过循环计算减少碳足迹，并提供本地供应以避免供应链风险。Citronics还支持企业打造可持续发展形象，现已获得多家公司信任。感兴趣的企业可预约咨询和预购。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕将旧手机改造成桌面电脑设备的可行性、价格合理性以及相关技术标准的讨论。

不同观点：
• DrNosferatu：支持减税以促进循环利用，但认为当前价格过高，需要下降一个数量级。
• neuroelectron：认为USB-C标准化有助于将旧手机改造成桌面电脑，并期待支持hub、USB外设及4K输出等功能。
• Bluestein：提出未来AI机器人可能自动处理电子废物，从中回收有用组件，实现真正的循环利用。
• Animats：指出需要大量相同型号的废弃手机才能实现这一想法，并提到Raspberry Pi本质上就是一种改装平板电脑。

data.title: Record DDoS pummels site with once-unimaginable 7.3Tbps of junk traffic
data.author: trustinmenowpls
data.article_summary: Cloudflare报告了一起创纪录的7.3Tbps分布式拒绝服务（DDoS）攻击，攻击者向单个IP地址的近22,000个端口发送大量数据，总计37.4TB。攻击主要通过用户数据报协议（UDP）数据包实现，利用其无需握手即可发送数据的特性，导致目标服务器过载。部分攻击还使用了反射技术，通过第三方服务器放大攻击流量。此次攻击利用了多种协议，并涉及Mirai僵尸网络。DDoS攻击的规模在过去几十年中不断增大，显示出日益严峻的网络安全威胁。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：DDoS攻击的现状、原因及潜在解决方案

不同观点：
• [1970-01-01] 认为直接从源头获取信息（如Cloudflare的博客）更为可靠，而不是通过二手报道或解读。该评论者对大量博客文章讨论技术问题的方式表示质疑，暗示这些讨论可能不够直接或准确。
  
• [jakub_g] 对QOTD协议被用于DDoS攻击表示惊讶，认为现代操作系统不应支持此类过时协议，并将其与"IP over Avian Carriers"（一种讽刺性的、不切实际的网络协议）相比较，暗示QOTD协议同样不实用且易被滥用。

• [londons_explore] 关注DDoS攻击的规模随着互联网用户和设备的增加而增长，并提出是否存在解决方案的疑问，表达了对DDoS攻击未来趋势的担忧。

• [losthobbies] 将DDoS攻击及相关问题归因于不可靠的IoT设备，暗示这些设备的安全性不足可能导致更严重的网络安全问题。

• [keygen_music] 以幽默方式回应，自称因未关闭智能冰箱而可能对DDoS攻击有所贡献，暗指物联网设备在DDoS攻击中的潜在角色。

• [shrubble] 关注DDoS攻击的流量规模，提到当前400Gbps和800Gbps的光学技术，并预测1.6Tbps即将到来，强调单个设备能够产生的攻击流量之大，令人担忧。

• [thih9] 对DDoS攻击规模持续增长的说法提出质疑，指出DDoS攻击历史不到三十年，并引用维基百科关于1996年首次DDoS攻击的例子，认为有关DDoS攻击规模不断增长的说法有误导性。

补充讨论：
• DDoS攻击的规模增长及其与互联网设备数量增长的关系是讨论的焦点之一，[londons_explore] 和 [shrubble] 都提到了这一趋势及其潜在影响。

• 不同评论者对技术细节的关注点不同，[jakub_g] 关注具体协议（QOTD）的实用性和安全性，[thih9] 则关注DDoS攻击历史的时间线。

• 评论中对物联网设备在DDoS攻击中的角色也有一定的讨论，[losthobbies] 和 [keygen_music] 都以幽默方式指出了物联网设备可能带来的安全问题。

争议焦点：DDoS攻击规模是否持续增长及其历史时间的准确性是[thih9]与其他评论者之间的主要争议点。
